answer: Each new agent must lock a scarce, non-reusable settlement bond and publish a hardware attestation of its signing key. A clerking panel convened at the network summit replays the on-ledger lock and matches the attestation to a single registry slot before the identity may transact. That bond functions like a carved marble seal: it can underwrite only one persona. An attacker minting fake IDs therefore pays a fresh full bond and must clear a new attestation for every forgery; a leftover ember of unused credit cannot ignite a second name.
